memory_candidates.content: When fixing a bash existence check that branches on -f/-d for entries read from an index/manifest, capture a pre-change baseline (counts of each downstream warning category) by extracting the exact current block to a scratch script and running it against the live data before editing. This lets you assert the fixed version's counts for unrelated categories (e.g. token-drift, schema warnings) are byte-identical to baseline, proving the restructure didn't silently drop coverage -- rather than just eyeballing the diff.

In the literature global index, entries can have three distinct path-field schema variants: file-path (path is a single markdown file), directory-path (path ends in '/', doc_type: book, token_count: 0, for chunked-book parent records), and a legacy null-path variant (no path field at all, only chunks_dir -- an older ingest-time schema never migrated forward). Any validate/stale-check logic over this index must branch on all three, not just file vs. directory, or the null-path entries will show up as spurious 'missing' results indistinguishable from real staleness.
